what: Penske Automotive runs car dealerships: about 350 of them in the United States and Britain, mostly premium brands, plus a large commercial truck dealership business and a stake in Penske Truck Leasing.
customers: Retail car buyers, mostly of premium brands, and trucking companies buying and servicing heavy trucks.
money: new and used car sales, parts and service
Freightliner and Western Star truck dealerships
its share of the truck leasing joint venture
moat: Franchise agreements with manufacturers, which are protected by state law and cannot simply be handed to a competitor, plus service bays that earn steadily whatever car sales do.
risks: A 2.9% net margin: dealerships make their money on volume and service, not on the cars
New vehicle gross profits have been falling back toward pre-2020 levels
Analysts' average target is about where the shares already trade
opportunities: 15 times earnings with revenue of $32.6B, and service and parts earn far more than the showroom
Revenue grew from $25.6B to $31.8B in four years
The truck leasing stake pays distributions that are unrelated to car retailing
watch: Gross profit per new vehicle, and service and parts revenue.
